_readme: Gold query set for BDRIS retrieval eval. Each entry has: query text, expected_category (always checked), and either expected_id (exact record must appear in top-K — used for faq/correction where a same-category-wrong-record hit is a real miss) or expected_id=null (category-level match is the honest bar — used for manual_walkthrough/rules2018/application_process where adjacent records legitimately overlap in content, and login_instructions where there's only 1 record so the distinction is moot). min_similarity is a soft floor: below it, treat as 'known-thin coverage' per the project's own lesson (low similarity signals missing coverage, not broken retrieval) rather than an automatic fail — the eval script should warn, not hard-fail, on a sub-threshold hit that still lands the right category/record. This is BDRIS's (and the project's) first gold query set — start small, expand once the pattern proves out on real runs.

queries.note: OUT-OF-SCOPE probe (revised) — weather has zero conceptual/vocabulary overlap with anything in a birth/death registration corpus, unlike the original 'mobile vs computer' probe which shared the word 'mobile' with mobile-number-rule records and produced a false fail (sim=0.60 against a 0.55 ceiling).
